lineage.summary: Originally invented by Modicon for its PLC family (Modbus name from MODicon-BUS). Defined the serial RTU and ASCII framings, the four data tables, and the core function-code set (Read Coils, Read/Write Holding Registers, etc.).
Modicon-proprietary high-speed HDLC token-passing peer-to-peer network carrying the same MODBUS PDU. Still referenced in V1.1b3 (Figure 1) but deprecated in favor of Modbus TCP.

Schneider Electric publishes the Open Modbus Specification, carrying the existing MODBUS PDU on a TCP/IP socket prefixed by a new 7-byte MBAP header. Reserved TCP port 502 assigned by IANA. Protocol_ID field = 0x0000 = MODBUS.
Schneider transfers stewardship of MODBUS to Modbus.org, an independent industry trade association. From this point all new versions are Modbus.org-released.

First Modbus.org release. Consolidated and re-edited the function-code reference into a single transport-agnostic document. Added Encapsulated Interface Transport (FC 0x2B) with MEI types 13 (CANopen) and 14 (Read Device Identification).
Minor errata + clarifications to V1.1; no new function codes.
Errata release that clarified Read Device Identification (FC 43 / MEI 14) object IDs, conformity levels, and Read Device ID codes 01/02/03/04.
Current stable release of the application protocol. Editorial cleanups; no new function codes. The version examined in this L doc set.

related_specifications.name: Modbus Messaging Implementation Guide V1.0a
related_specifications.description: Companion document defining the Modbus TCP framing (MBAP header) and TCP-specific behavior (port 502, Transaction ID, Protocol ID, Length, Unit ID). Referenced from V1.1b3 §1.1.

related_specifications.name: Modbus over Serial Line Specification & Implementation Guide V1.02
related_specifications.description: Companion document defining the RTU and ASCII serial framing rules (T3.5 silent line, CRC-16-Modbus, LRC, ':', CR LF).

related_specifications.name: CiA CANopen General Reference
related_specifications.description: Encapsulated under FC 0x2B MEI Type 13; payload format defined by CAN-in-Automation (CiA).

backward_compat_traps.trap: A client that puts the user-facing register number directly into the PDU Starting Address field reads one register past the intended one. Always Starting_Address = user_number - 1.
FC 0x05 Write Single Coil rejects any Output Value other than 0xFF00 / 0x0000 with exception 0x03 ILLEGAL DATA VALUE. The value is not '1' / '0' — it is '0xFF00' / '0x0000'.

backward_compat_traps.on_wire_order: Low byte first, high byte second.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Many implementations debug a CRC mismatch by checking the wrong byte order. The CRC on the wire is little-endian even though all data quantities in the PDU are big-endian.

backward_compat_traps.normal_response: Function Code byte echoes the request function code unchanged.
backward_compat_traps.exception_response: Function Code byte = original function code OR 0x80.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A client that ignores the MSB of the response Function Code mis-parses an exception response as a normal response and dereferences invalid Data bytes.

backward_compat_traps.modbus: Protocol ID field in MBAP must be 0x0000 to identify MODBUS.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Reusing the TCP socket for a different protocol while Protocol ID != 0 is reserved for future use; non-MODBUS payloads are silently invalid.

backward_compat_traps.serial_only: FC 0x07 Read Exception Status, 0x08 Diagnostics, 0x0B Get Comm Event Counter, 0x0C Get Comm Event Log, 0x11 Report Server ID.
backward_compat_traps.trap: These FCs are not supported on Modbus TCP per spec. A TCP server that responds to them is non-conforming; a TCP client that issues them gets exception 0x01 ILLEGAL FUNCTION from a conforming server.
Different FCs have different maxima; copying a 2000-coil quantity into a register-read request triggers exception 0x03.
Implementing one of these for a private feature breaks future MODBUS compliance; use User-Defined ranges 65..72 or 100..110 instead.

fields.version_naming_history_note: Modbus.org maintains the application protocol document on https://modbus.org. Version 1.1b3 is the current April-26-2012 release used by virtually all modern MODBUS implementations. The companion Modbus Messaging Implementation Guide V1.0a (TCP) and Modbus over Serial Line V1.02 (RTU/ASCII) documents are required reading for any TCP- or serial-specific implementation work.
